---
title: "Calibration limits (4.1–4.4)"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
box::use(show = projlib/show, util = projlib/msdial_utils)
tr <- tut$to_report
# best <- tr[["best normalization"]]
best <- "loess_norm"   # The app's default method ("best normalization" is not used for now)
mat_id <- util$mat_id_of_blank_subtracted(best)
lst <- tut$proc[[mat_id]]
b1 <- names(lst)[1]
batch <- lst[[b1]]
```

Page 4 of the app, **Calibration and quantification**, turns the signals of the targeted compounds
into concentrations. At the top you choose the **normalization method** (`r tut$method_labels[[best]]`
is preselected) and the **batch**; the tables and figures follow. The
examples below show batch `r b1`. With several batches, the batch choice also has **Global**: the
global curve of every compound (fitted on the calibration points of all batches) in table 4.1 and
figure 4.5, for comparison only; the concentrations are calculated per batch, so figures 4.6 and 4.7
are empty then.

How a calibration curve is made, in short:

1. The **zero calibrant** (`Cal0`) gives two signal thresholds: 3× and 10× its mean signal (or its
   mean plus 3 and 10 standard deviations).
2. The **LOD** is the lowest calibration level whose mean signal is above the first threshold, the
   **LLOQ** the lowest above the second (and, with the RSD% option, with an RSD% of at most 20%).
3. The curve is fitted from the LLOQ upwards: linear or quadratic, weighted 1, 1/x or 1/x², the
   combination with the highest R².
4. The **ULOQ** is the top of the linear range of the calibration levels, looked for from the
   highest level down (see 4.1 and the next chapter).

## 4.1 Calibration curve limits

```{r}
#| label: table-4-2
# The rows of the app's table 4.1 (the same function), then the row colours from its helper columns
rd_all <- SumExp::row_df(tut$raw)
names_tbl <- tibble::tibble(feature_id = rownames(rd_all), feature_name = rd_all$feature_name)
n_batches <- length(unique(as.character(SumExp::col_df(tut$raw)$batch_id)))
t41 <- show$page4_table41(batch, b1, tr, best, names_tbl, n_batches)
t41$state <- dplyr::case_when(t41$is_removed ~ "removed", t41$is_bad ~ "bad", t41$is_global ~ "global", TRUE ~ "")
t41 <- t41[setdiff(names(t41), c("is_global", "is_bad", "is_removed"))]
DT::datatable(t41, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none", escape = setdiff(names(t41), "Notes"),
              caption = htmltools::HTML(show$calib_notes_legend_html()),
              options = list(dom = "ft", paging = FALSE, scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "420px", scrollCollapse = TRUE,
                             columnDefs = list(list(targets = ncol(t41) - 1, visible = FALSE)))) |>
  DT::formatStyle("state", target = "row",
                  backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c("bad", "global", "removed"),
                                                   c("lightcoral", "lightblue", "#D9D9D9")))
```

One row per targeted compound with its limits in the chosen batch. In the app, **select a row**
(or step with the arrow keys ↑ / ↓) to show that compound in figures 4.5–4.7.

**How to read it**

- **The row colour** tells the curve used for the compound in this batch: the batch's own (white),
  the curve of all batches together (*global curve*, blue rows, also the globe icon in *Notes*), or
  none (red rows).
- **LOD and LLOQ** are calibration levels; values below them are replaced or reported as
  *n.d.* / *n.q.* (see 4.6).
- **Highest cal. conc.** is the highest level the curve is fitted on; the **ULOQ** is the top of the
  linear range, looked for among all calibration levels from the LLOQ up, whatever the settings. The
  ULOQ is lower when the top levels bend away from the line and the curve was not cut there (option
  *Enforce ULOQ*), or was cut but keeps the minimum number of calibration levels. It is higher when
  *Optimize calibration curves* ended the curve below the top level (the curve only needs to reach
  the highest sample). A quadratic curve has no ULOQ.
- **Notes** show an icon per kind of note; **hover an icon** for the full text:

```{r}
#| label: table-note-icons
#| results: asis
cats <- util$calib_note_categories
meaning <- c(
  notvalid = "No valid curve: e.g. too few levels above the LLOQ, no signal, or R² below the minimum. The row is red.",
  global = "The batch's own curve is not valid, or the batch has too few replicates: the global curve is used.",
  uloq = "Linear range: levels above the ULOQ, which were cut off or are above the linear range.",
  detection = "Detection in the samples: not detected in any study sample, or detected but below the LLOQ (not exported).",
  rtrange = "Elutes more than 1 min outside the retention time range of the internal standards: no internal standard nearby, so the RT-based normalizations (LOESS, Closest RT) are extrapolated.",
  removed = "Removed before calibration by the blank filter or the QC RSD% filter. The row is grey."
)
# The app's icon of each category (without the hidden text the tables carry for searching)
icon <- vapply(names(cats), function(k) {
  sub('<span style="display:none">.*$', "", show$calib_notes_html(tibble::tibble(!!k := cats[[k]]), size = 20))
}, "")
cat(paste0("  - ", icon, " **", cats, "**: ", meaning[names(cats)], collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

The exported tables have the same notes in full, as text.

## 4.2 Calibration per batch

```{r}
#| label: table-4-2-batches
bs_tbl <- show$page4_batch_status(lst, tr, best)
htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$style(htmltools::HTML(paste(
    ".q-bdot{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:1px;min-width:18px;height:18px;padding:0 4px;margin:1px 2px 1px 0;border-radius:9px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;line-height:1;box-sizing:border-box;cursor:help;vertical-align:middle}",
    ".q-bdot-ok{background:#12B76A;color:#fff}",
    ".q-bdot-global{background:#E0F0FA;color:#0072B2;border:1px solid #0072B2}",
    ".q-bdot-failed{background:#FDECEA;color:#B42318;border:1px solid #B42318}",
    ".q-bdot-removed,.q-bdot-none{background:#D9D9D9;color:#555}"))),
  DT::datatable(bs_tbl[, c("Chemical Name", "Calibration per batch")], rownames = FALSE, selection = "none",
                escape = "Chemical Name",
                options = list(dom = "ft", paging = FALSE, ordering = FALSE, scrollY = "300px", scrollCollapse = TRUE))
)
```

One row per targeted compound with the calibration of every batch, one dot each with the batch in it
(hover a dot for the details). This is the same for every batch you choose.

- **Green**: the batch's own curve is used.
- **Blue globe**: the batch's curve is not valid; the global curve is used.
- **Red globe**: neither the batch's curve nor the global curve is valid: no concentrations.
- **Grey**: removed before calibration (blank filter or QC RSD% filter), at the end.

## 4.3 Calibration curve samples

```{r}
#| label: table-4-1
v <- util$spiked_conc_pts(batch$calcurve)
tut_table(as.data.frame(table(v[!is.na(v)]), check.names = FALSE) |>
            stats::setNames(c("Concentration", "Samples")), height = "300px")
```

The number of calibration samples per concentration level in the chosen batch: the replicates the
curve of this batch is fitted on.

## 4.4 Quantified compounds per batch

```{r}
#| label: table-4-3
tut_table(purrr::map_dfr(lst, function(x) {
  se <- x$concn[SumExp::row_df(x$concn)$has_proper_range %in% TRUE, ]
  tibble::tibble(Compounds =sum(rowSums(!is.na(se[["conc"]])) > 0))
}, .id = "Batch"), height = "200px")
```

The number of compounds per batch with a valid calibration curve **and** concentrations in the
samples. Compounds without any study sample at or above the LLOQ are not quantified and not
exported.
